haolong:study:1.title: Cellular-level preservation of cutaneous spikes in an Early Cretaceous iguanodontian dinosaur (Nature Ecology & Evolution, 2026)

facts.statement: Haolong was described by Huang and colleagues.
Haolong lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Barremian age.
The type locality for Haolong is the Yixian Formation.
Haolong fossils have been found in China.
Haolong is classified as an iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur.
The genus Haolong contains only one known species, Haolong dongi.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Haolong dongi

facts.statement: Haolong is known from a nearly complete, articulated skeleton that preserves skin structures.
facts.quote: known from a nearly complete, articulated skeleton with preserved integumentary structures

facts.statement: The specific name dongi honors the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.
facts.quote: The specific name, dongi, honors Dong Zhiming, a prominent Chinese paleontologist.

facts.statement: Haolong is known from a single holotype specimen identified as AGM 16793.
facts.quote: Haolong is known from a single specimen, the holotype AGM 16793

facts.statement: The known specimen of Haolong is a nearly complete juvenile measuring about 2.45 meters in length.
facts.quote: It represents a nearly complete juvenile about 2.45 m long.

facts.statement: The specimen preserves scales mixed with hollow, keratinous spines that are preserved at the cellular level.
facts.quote: The specimen preserves remains of the integumentary system, which consists of scales interspersed with hollow, keratinous spines preserved down to the nuclear level.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the spines may have functioned for protection, thermoregulation, or tactile sensing.
facts.quote: They may have served as protection from predators, as thermoregulatory aids, or as tactile structures.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether adult Haolong possessed the same spines as the juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Since the specimen is a juvenile, it is unknown if adults also possessed similar structures.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Haolong as an early-diverging member of the Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: They recovered Haolong as an early-diverging member of the Hadrosauroidea

facts.statement: The genus Haolong was established by Huang et al. in 2026.
Haolong originated in the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) and was found in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: originario del Cretácico Inferior (Barremiense) encontrado en la formación Yixian de Liaoning, China

facts.statement: Haolong is placed as an early-diverging hadrosauroid, branching after a European clade containing Brighstoneus, Cariocecus, and Comptonatus.
facts.quote: Recuperaron a Haolong como un miembro de divergencia temprana de los Hadrosauroidea, ramificándose después de un clado europeo compuesto por Brighstoneus, Cariocecus y Comptonatus

facts.statement: Haolong lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The name Haolong translates to "spiny dragon" in Mandarin Chinese.
rejected.quote: The generic name, Haolong, comes from Mandarin Chinese and translates to "spiny dragon"
